notes: Profile: mid-to-large marketplace specializing in verticals (home goods + seasonal apparel). Catalog ~12M SKUs with heavy spikes during holiday windows.
Primary ask: improve semantic relevance for long-tail queries and product reranking for conversions while holding cost/query under strict threshold during scale.
Current stack: hybrid search—Elastic for primary retrieval, in-house reranker (BERT-based) for top-50 results. Using off-the-shelf embeddings batch-indexed nightly; cold start issues for new SKUs.

Performance targets: 95th pctile search latency (end-to-end rerank) <= 200ms for NA region on typical traffic; 95th pctile during peak burst <= 400ms acceptable with graceful degradation to lower-cost model variants.
Cost target: average cost per user query (retrieve+embed+rerank) target <= $0.0025; current internal cost ~ $0.006 per query at peak with BERT reranker.
Indexing scale: want incremental embeddings pipeline for ~1k updates/min during promos; full reindex monthly. Interested in Redwood Optimize recommendations for quantization + batching to shave cost.
Data residency: must keep PII and purchase history in VPC; embeddings can be stored encrypted in Redwood's dedicated pool but require KMS integration.
Security: SSO (Okta), SCIM, audit logs required. Legal asked about data retention and ability to purge vectors tied to EU users.
Notes from AE (Maya): 'They're very cost-sensitive around holiday windows — need clear burst pricing and fallbacks.'

Notes from SE (Diego): ran small baseline test on hosted API — embedding latency 12ms median, reranker CPU-bound, end-to-end 280ms for 50-result rerank. Need Dedicated GPU nodes to hit 200ms p95 and cost targets.

POC proposal: 6-week evaluation. Phase 1: 1M SKU index, retrieval+embedding+rerank pipeline, run query set (10k queries) including long-tail & promo phrases. Phase 2: simulate 10x seasonal burst for concurrency and measure cost per Q and tail latency.
Stakeholders: Head of Search (Priya Sethi), CTO (Liam O'Connor), Head of Ops (Ellen Zhang). Procurement lead (Tom Beck) is focused on SLA and SOC2 evidence.
Commercial: prefer committed Dedicated pool for baseline traffic + burst credits. We proposed 3-month pilot pricing and uplift for Black Friday month.
Integration notes: will provide sandbox S3 export of product catalog + feature signals (CTR, conversions) for rerank training. Prefer redwood client in Kubernetes sidecar for inference.
Risks: training reranker on proprietary signals increases ops complexity; if we can't meet cost/query they will consider Elastic + third-party rerankers or in-house distillation.
Open questions: how Redwood handles KV cache invalidation on SKU updates, quantization options for CPU fallback, and guaranteed fallback model mapping during capacity faults.
